rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for putting on an act or pretending to hold a view.

example.english: I don't really think that, so you don't need to posture here.
example.traditional: 我唔係真係咁諗，你唔使喺度扮嘢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 zan1 hai6 gam3 nam2 nei5 m4 sai2 hai2 dou6 baan6 je5

rows.note: Use this when someone is deliberately striking a political or public stance for appearances, especially for the media.

example.english: They deliberately posture in front of the cameras so reporters can film them.
example.traditional: 為咗畀記者影到，佢哋特登喺鏡頭前扮姿態。
example.jyutping: wai6 zo2 bei2 gei3 ze2 jing2 dou3 keoi5 dei6 dak6 dang1 hai2 geng3 tau4 cin4 baan6 zi1 taai3

rows.note: For physical body position, this is the all-purpose choice.

example.english: Your posture is very good when you sit so straight.
example.traditional: 你坐得咁直，姿勢好好喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 co5 dak1 gam3 zik6 zi1 sai3 hou2 hou2 wo3

rows.note: Use this for someone’s social or political stance on an issue.

example.english: The government’s posture on this issue is still unclear.
example.traditional: 政府喺呢件事上面嘅立場仲未清楚。
example.jyutping: zing3 fu2 hai2 ni1 gin6 si6 soeng6 min6 ge3 laap6 coeng4 zung6 mei6 cing1 co2

rows.note: Use this for someone’s attitude or manner towards another person or situation, rather than a position on an issue.

example.english: Her posture toward the new colleague is quite friendly.
example.traditional: 佢對新同事嘅態度幾好。
example.jyutping: keoi5 deoi3 san1 tung4 si6 ge3 taai3 dou6 gei2 hou2
